acceptanceCriteria.criterion: README.md on merged main contains the new line `Stage 3 smoke proof: Legion workflow end-to-end.`
acceptanceCriteria.negativeControl: grep -F for a line that was NOT appended must exit 1 (no false match).
acceptanceCriteria.proofCommand: legion gh -- api repos/sjawhar/legion-smoke/contents/README.md --jq '.content' | base64 -d | grep -F 'Stage 3 smoke proof: Legion workflow end-to-end.'  (run against the merge commit / main after merge). Pre-merge, verify locally with: cd -- "$LEGION_WORKSPACE" && jj -R "$LEGION_WORKSPACE" file show README.md | grep -F 'Stage 3 smoke proof: Legion workflow end-to-end.'
acceptanceCriteria.surface: The sjawhar/legion-smoke Git repository README.md on the merged main branch (production-like surface = the real repo on GitHub).

acceptanceCriteria.criterion: The PR that adds the line is reviewed and merged under branch-protection rules.
acceptanceCriteria.negativeControl: Before approval/merge, the same query shows state=OPEN and no mergeCommit, confirming the gate is real.
acceptanceCriteria.proofCommand: legion gh -- pr view <n> --repo sjawhar/legion-smoke --json state,reviewDecision,mergeCommit --jq '{state, reviewDecision, mergeCommit: .mergeCommit.oid}'  (expect state=MERGED, reviewDecision=APPROVED, non-null mergeCommit).

implementation.ordering: Single-file edit -> commit -> push -> PR. No dependencies; one implementer pass.
steps: Bind to $LEGION_WORKSPACE; confirm README.md exists at repo root (spec Errors: stop and report if missing).
Append the single exact line to the end of README.md; no trailing edits elsewhere.
Commit on the issue branch, set bookmark legion/S392088555-1, push, and open the PR with body line `Dispatch: S392088555-1`.
If review requests one additional appended line, append it to the same README.md in the same PR (in scope).

integration.conflictPolicy: On conflict, rebase on current main and re-append the single line; never force-overwrite unrelated content (spec Errors).

nonGoals: No new files (spec Rejected: a new file is out of scope).
No source/build/config file edits (spec Rejected: risks CI and obscures the proof).

implement: none: reviewed the system-prompt <skills> list (dispatch, envoy, legion-architect, legion-controller, legion-oracle, legion-retro, legion-worker) and the fixture repo (README.md, smoke/, stage3-proof.txt) for AGENTS.md/verification norms; no repository has an AGENTS.md and no domain agent skill drives a plain one-line README append. legion-worker governs the worker process itself, not this surface.
review: none: same review as above; no code-quality or review skill is specific to a one-line markdown append. Reviewer applies the generic Legion review gate (single-file diff, byte-exact line, no stray files).
test: none: same review as above; the change has no build/test suite and no test-surface skill applies. Proof is file content on merged main and PR review/merge state, driven directly via `legion gh` / `jj file show`.

focus: Exactly one file (README.md) changed; diff adds exactly the one specified line (or two if review asked for a second).
No source/build/config files touched; no new files created.
Appended line text is byte-exact: `Stage 3 smoke proof: Legion workflow end-to-end.`

summary: Append exactly one line to README.md at the repo root: `Stage 3 smoke proof: Legion workflow end-to-end.` One file, one line, no code paths touched. Prove on merged main + PR review/merge.

targetFiles.change: Append the single line `Stage 3 smoke proof: Legion workflow end-to-end.` to the end of the file. Preserve all existing content; no other edits. If review asks for one more appended line, add it to this same file in the same PR (in scope per spec Requirements).

testing.acceptance1: Open README.md on merged main and confirm the appended line is present (see AC1 proofCommand).
testing.acceptance2: Confirm the PR shows an approving review and a merge commit (see AC2 proofCommand).
testing.notes: No unit/CI suite exists in this fixture repo; proof is the file content on main and the PR review/merge state. Tester re-runs the implementer's AC1/AC2 commands on the real surface.
